title: Mitosis vs meiosis: two ways a cell divides
examples: What is the difference between mitosis and meiosis?
How many cells does meiosis make?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: Mitosis copies; meiosis halves and mixes

explain.say: Here is a puzzle for you. Your cells have 46 chromosomes. If a sperm and an egg each had 46, a baby would have 92! Something must stop that. Let's compare the two ways cells divide.

draw.text: Mitosis vs meiosis: two ways a cell divides

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Mitosis copies; meiosis halves and mixes

explain.say: Look at the left side: mitosis. One division makes 2 cells, each with all 46 chromosomes, identical to the first. It is the copy machine for growing and healing. Where in your body might this happen today?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Mitosis copies; meiosis halves and mixes

explain.say: Now the right side: meiosis. It divides twice and makes 4 cells, each with only 23 chromosomes. These are gametes, which means sex cells: sperm and eggs. How many cells does meiosis make?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Mitosis copies; meiosis halves and mixes

explain.say: See the last line on each side. Mitosis cells are identical, but in meiosis the chromosomes are shuffled, so every gamete is a bit different. That is why brothers and sisters do not look exactly alike. Can you see why?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Mitosis copies; meiosis halves and mixes

explain.say: So 23 from mum plus 23 from dad makes 46 again. Brilliant! Wow fact: one person can make over 8 million different mixes of chromosomes, even before any swapping of pieces.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Mitosis copies; meiosis halves and mixes

faq.a: Mitosis makes two identical cells with the full number of chromosomes. It is used for growth, repair and asexual reproduction.
Meiosis makes gametes, which are sperm and egg cells in animals, or pollen and ovules in plants. Each gamete has half the usual number of chromosomes.

faq.q: Why do gametes have only 23 chromosomes?
faq.a: When a sperm and an egg join at fertilisation, 23 plus 23 gives 46, the normal number. If gametes had 46, the number would double every generation.

faq.q: Why are the cells from meiosis all different?
faq.a: In meiosis, each pair of chromosomes is split up in a random way, and pairs can swap pieces, called crossing over. So every gamete gets a unique mix of genes.
asks: Why are brothers and sisters different?

faq.q: What do diploid and haploid mean?
faq.a: Diploid means a cell has two sets of chromosomes, 46 in humans. Haploid means one set, 23 in humans, as in sperm and eggs.

facts: Human body cells have 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs; human gametes have 23.
Independent assortment alone gives 2 to the power 23, over 8 million, possible chromosome combinations in a human gamete.

quiz.say: How many cells does meiosis produce from one cell?
quiz.show: How many cells does meiosis produce from one cell?
quiz.why: Meiosis has two divisions, so one cell becomes four gametes.

wrong.0: Two cells is the result of mitosis.
wrong.2: 46 is the number of chromosomes in a body cell, not a number of cells.

quiz.say: Which process repairs a cut on your hand?
quiz.show: Which process repairs a cut on your hand?
quiz.why: Mitosis makes identical new skin cells to replace damaged ones.

wrong.0: Meiosis only makes sperm and eggs.
wrong.2: Fertilisation is the joining of a sperm and an egg.
